newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian wool prices firmer in week.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian wool prices firmer in week.

text.p: The Australian wool market continued to firm at auctions in Sydney and Melbourne this week, Wesfarmers Dalgety said in its weekly report on Friday.
The eastern market indicator rose a cent to 615 cents a kg.

"Exporters expect demand for wool will increase as European processors return from summer holidays and supply increases over the next few weeks," the Australian Council of Wool Exporters said in a weekly report. The council said this week's offering in Sydney consisted predominantly of premium 22 micron and finer wool drawn from the Newcastle region.
This type of wool continues to be both in short supply and keenly sought after by several buyers with commitments to supply manufacturers, the council said.

In the futures market, the 21 micron contract for the week ended 29 August 1996 a total of 147 contracts were traded. The October 96 contract closed 14 cents up at 769 cents a kg clean. Sales next week are in Sydney and Fremantle with 69,468 bales on offer.
